'''''Heptapleurum actinophyllum''''' (formerly ''Schefflera actinophylla'') is a tree in the family [[Araliaceae]].{{r|powo|GRIN}} It is native to tropical [[rainforest]]s and [[gallery forest]]s in northern and northeastern [[Queensland]] coasts and the [[Northern Territory]] of Australia, as well as [[New Guinea]] and [[Java]]. Common names include '''Australian umbrella tree''', '''Queensland umbrella tree''', '''octopus tree''' and '''amate'''.

==Description==
''Heptapleurum actinophyllum'' is an evergreen tree growing to {{convert|15|m|ft|-1|abbr=in}} tall. It has palmately compound medium green leaves in groups of seven leaflets. It is usually multi-trunked, and the flowers develop at the top of the tree.{{r|plantnet}} It often grows as a [[hemiepiphyte]] on other rainforest trees.{{r|martin2005|p=43}} It produces [[raceme]]s up to {{convert|2|m|ft|round=0.5|abbr=in}} long containing up to 1,000 small red flowers. Flowering begins in early summer and typically continues for several months.

The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''actinophyllum'' means "with radiating leaves".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for Gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=London|isbn=978-1-84533-731-5|page=224}}</ref>

==Ecology==
The up to 1,000 flowers produced by the plant generate large amounts of nectar, attracting nectar-eating birds that pollinate them. The fruits are eaten by many birds and animals including [[musky rat-kangaroo]]s, [[red-legged pademelon]]s and [[spectacled flying fox]]es.{{r|beasley2006}} Its leaves are a favourite food of the [[Bennett's tree-kangaroo]].{{r|martin2005}}{{r|beasley2009|p=105}}

==Cultivation==
It is commonly grown in mild to warm climates as a decorative tree in larger gardens and, when mature, it has red spikes of flowers with up to 20 racemes which develop in summer or early autumn. Propagation is by seed or cuttings. It prefers well-drained soil and only needs occasional watering and feeding to thrive. It is, however, an aggressive plant and its roots can dominate surrounding soil. In some areas (e.g., Florida and Hawaii, USA), it is an invasive weed and therefore planting is highly unadvised.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.state.hi.us/dlnr/dofaw/hortweeds/species/schact.htm|title=Hawaii's Most Invasive Horticultural Plants octopus tree ''Schefflera actinophylla''|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120203100229/http://www.state.hi.us/dlnr/dofaw/hortweeds/species/schact.htm|archive-date=3 February 2012}}</ref>

With a minimum temperature of {{convert|13|C|F}}, juvenile specimens are grown in temperate regions as houseplants.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=London|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|page=1136}}</ref> This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Schefflera actinophylla''|url=
https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16795/Schefflera-actinophylla/Details |access-date=12 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=95 
|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>
